reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable space; the zero-dimensional case is included. Let V:E→ℝ be twice continuously differentiable, α,β be nonnegative real numbers, and η a real number. Assume α>0, α≤β, and, for every x,v∈E, α||v||²≤D(DV)(x)[v][v]≤β||v||². Assume η>0 and βη≤1.

Define c(y,r)=y−η∇V(r). For every real t and z=(x,v)∈E×E define Φ(y,r,t,z)=(c(y,r)+cos(t)(x−c(y,r))+√η sin(t)v, −sin(t)/√η (x−c(y,r))+cos(t)v). Define g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S(r,(x,v))=(x,v−[2⟨v,g_r(x)⟩/||g_r(x)||²]g_r(x)), and λ(r,(x,v))=√η max(0,⟨v,g_r(x)⟩). Real division is total and a quotient with zero denominator is zero. For u≥0 define Λ(y,r,z,u)=∫₀ᵘ λ(r,Φ(y,r,s,z)) ds. For e≥0 let τ(y,r,z,e)=inf{u≥0:Λ(y,r,z,u)−e≥0}, with value +∞ for the empty set, as the nonnegative-time hittingAfter function starting at 0. Write f(a)=a if a is finite and f(+∞)=0.

Let ℛ=(ℝ≥0×(E×E))⊔{stopped}. Define next(y,r,e,stopped)=stopped. At an active record (a,z), next is stopped when τ(y,r,z,e)=+∞; otherwise next=(a+f(τ(y,r,z,e)),S(r,Φ(y,r,f(τ(y,r,z,e)),z))). For an initial state z₀ and sequence e:N→ℝ≥0 define record₀=(0,z₀) and recordₖ₊₁=next(y,r,eₖ,recordₖ).

Let P be the countable product, on real sequences w:N→ℝ, of the rate-one exponential law on ℝ. Define ε(w)ₖ=max(wₖ,0) as a nonnegative real. Fix any y,r∈E, z₀∈E×E and n∈N. Put Hist=ℛ^{Fin(n+1)}, last=n, H(w)ⱼ=recordⱼ(y,r,z₀,ε(w)) for j=0,...,n, and μ=H_*P.

For q=(a,s)∈ℛ×ℝ define W(y,r,q)=τ(y,r,z,max(s,0)) when a=(b,z) is active, and W=0 when a=stopped. Define T(y,r,q)=f(W(y,r,q)), interpreted in ℝ. Define ρ(y,r,((b,z),s))=ofReal(λ(r,Φ(y,r,s,z)) exp(−Λ(y,r,z,max(s,0)))), and ρ(y,r,(stopped,s))=0, where ofReal embeds the nonnegative part into [0,+∞].

Then W and ρ are measurable on ℛ×ℝ, and ρ(q)≠+∞ for every q.

Moreover, for every fixed measurable function d:Hist→ℝ≥0, define D(h,s)=ρ(y,r,(h_last,s)) if 0<s<d(h), and D(h,s)=0 otherwise. Let K be the constant Lebesgue-time kernel with density D. Define
B={w:0<W(y,r,(record_n(y,r,z₀,ε(w)),w_n))<d(H(w))},
where both comparisons are in ℝ≥0∪{+∞}. Define X(w)=(H(w),T(y,r,(record_n(y,r,z₀,ε(w)),w_n))) and ν=(μ⊗Lebesgue).withDensity((h,s)↦D(h,s)).

The function (h,s)↦D(h,s) is measurable; for every history h, K(h)=Lebesgue.withDensity(D(h,·)); K is a finite kernel with a uniform finite bound on all fiber masses, and specifically K(h)(ℝ)≤1 for every h. The set B is measurable, X is measurable, X_*(P restricted to B)=ν, and ν(Hist×ℝ)≤1.

Finally, for every measurable F:Hist×ℝ→[0,+∞], the function h↦∫ F(h,s)D(h,s) ds (the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral) is measurable; and for every measurable A⊆Hist,
∫_{B∩H⁻¹(A)} F(X(w)) dP(w)=∫_A [∫_R F(h,s)D(h,s) ds] dμ(h).
All measure restrictions and integrals here are unnormalized.

objects.reference: xRef=r is an arbitrary fixed element of E; y is another arbitrary fixed element
objects.accumulated_rate: Λ(y,r,z,u)=real interval Bochner integral from 0 to u of λ(r,Φ(y,r,s,z)), u:NNReal
objects.wait: τ=nonnegative-time hittingAfter of Λ−e into [0,∞), starting at 0, with values WithTop NNReal
objects.finite_projection: untopD 0 retains finite wait and returns zero at top
objects.record: Nat.rec from active time zero and z₀; update k uses threshold e k
objects.product_law: Measure.infinitePi of expMeasure 1 over real sequences
objects.history: H(w) consists of record indices 0 through n inclusive; record n uses only coordinates 0 through n−1
objects.wait_observation: For active record (a,z) paired with real s, τ(y,r,z,toNNReal(s)); stopped record gives zero; accumulated absolute time a is ignored
objects.time_observation: Real coercion of finite projection of wait_observation
objects.density_observation: Active: ofReal(λ(r,Φ(y,r,s,z))*exp(−Λ(y,r,z,toNNReal(s)))); stopped: zero. The flow uses raw s even if s<0

objects.joint_observation: X(w)=(H(w), real finite-projected next waiting observation using coordinate w n)
objects.joint_measure: ν=(μ.prod volume).withDensity D, μ=Measure.map H P

conclusion.precise_mass_reading: The mass bounds are integrated total measure bounds. Density may exceed one pointwise. No equality-to-one assertion occurs.

scopes.fixed_vs_random: d is a fixed measurable history function universally quantified outside sample evaluation. d(H(w)) is random by composition; no independent external random function, extra random cap, or extra randomness is quantified.
scopes.histories: Hist includes all tagged record sequences, with no consistency constraint; pointwise fiber conclusions apply to all of them.
scopes.common_parameters: All lets and conclusions share the same V,α,β,η,y,xRef,z₀,n as applicable.
scopes.cap_independence: W and ρ and their measurability/finiteness are stated before and independently of the cap quantifier.
scopes.endpoint_conventions: Rate integral uses 0..u; hitting target is closed [0,∞), allowing τ=0; D and B both use strict lower and upper bounds; no contribution at wait zero or at wait=d(h).
scopes.no_normalization: P.restrict B, μ restrictions, kernel fibers, ν, and all displayed integrals remain unnormalized.

branches.finite_wait: Update accumulates finite wait and reflects the flowed state; T equals that wait.
branches.zero_wait: Λ(0)=0 and e=0 give τ=0; the update still applies S at Φ(0,z)=z, with no positive-time guard in recursion. B excludes zero waits.
branches.top_wait: The next record becomes stopped. W retains top for an active input with no hit; T defaults to zero at top. B excludes top because d is finite.
branches.stopped: Stopped state is absorbing under next; W=T=ρ=0. If the last history record is stopped then D=0 and the sequence does not belong to B.
branches.zero_cap: d(h)=0 makes D(h,·)=0; B excludes sequences whose history has zero cap.
branches.zero_gradient_difference: Total division makes the reflection velocity correction zero when g_r(x)=0; S leaves that state unchanged and its instantaneous rate is zero.
branches.zero_dimension: Allowed by all instances. All vectors and gradients vanish; rates and accumulated rates vanish; positive thresholds have top waits while threshold zero has zero wait. The strict-event measure and capped density vanish.
branches.n_zero: History has one initial record; fresh coordinate is w 0.
branches.negative_raw_coordinate: toNNReal converts it to zero for W and Λ; the raw density's Φ is evaluated at the negative real. The capped density D is zero at every nonpositive real.

flow: No additional numerical rescaling of trigonometric time
hessian: α and β bound the Hessian quadratic form; no coefficient 1/2 is present
cap: d may depend on the entire finite history, and therefore on the fixed n/history type; it has no external random argument
